question: Is the physical even-moment hierarchy low-order enough to provide useful fair/intermediate LER intervals before any replica-transfer implementation is attempted?
scope: No-new-sampling feasibility diagnostic. Exact L3 tables and frozen L5 posterior records only; no analytic curve, fit, threshold, decoder comparison, or contraction tuning.

estimand.truth_check: Each exact or empirical Bayes risk must lie inside its own moment interval at every N.

uncertainty.L5: pointwise nonparametric bootstrap 95% interval for the remainder width, resampling independent physical records

primary_gate.pass: At N=32 every primary cell has point width <=.01 and bootstrap-95 upper width <=.0125.
primary_gate.interpretation: Passing only establishes that low-order physical moments are a potentially useful compression target; it does not solve how to calculate them analytically.

secondary_diagnostics: Exact L3 and near-directed L5 cells diagnose bias and size dependence but cannot rescue a failed primary gate.
stop_rule: If any primary cell fails, close moment compression and do not implement replica transfer. If all pass, retain exactly one future interface-design step for physical R-to-1 moments.
compute_budget: Twelve exact L3 enumerations, seven frozen L5 files and 4000 bootstrap replicates per L5 cell; no new physical records.
